summary: American crypto entrepreneur Sam Bankman-Fried used effective-altruism branding, celebrity ads and friendly press to build the FTX exchange and Alameda Research, which collapsed in 2022 after customer funds were misused.

evidence.note: Birth in 1992 on the Stanford campus and his professor parents
Meets MacAskill at MIT and adopts effective altruism and earn-to-give
Leaves Jane Street in 2017 to trade crypto, start of the main events
Founds Alameda with EA colleagues after the Asian bitcoin arbitrage
Launches FTX in 2019 with Alameda trading profits
Company moves to Hong Kong and then the Bahamas, buys a mansion there
Long segment mocking the Sequoia puff piece and the pitch that won investors
Arena naming rights, athlete ads and sponsorships used to build confidence
Bankruptcy filing and the new CEO's verdict on the missing controls in 2022
Large donations to both parties to shape crypto regulation

notes: Recorded days after the November 2022 collapse, so it borders on current-affairs, but it tells his life story from birth, hence deep-dive. Bahamas listed first as the seat of FTX where the collapse happened; victims were worldwide. No theme for effective altruism or longtermism; tech-internet used for the Silicon Valley ideology angle.
